utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.text: Yes, then I'll have to look at that in further details to know exactly what that requires. Thank you for putting it on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the translation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The -- Witness, before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make the solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Witness, you'll first be examined by Mr. Lukic. You'll find Mr. Lukic to your left. Mr. Lukic is counsel for the Prosecution -- for the Defence. Mr. Lukic, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Probably if I do my job badly I could be for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I'm doing my job badly at this moment, Mr. Lukic. That's the situation. Apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Kijac.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask the usher to provide Mr. Kijac with his statement in hard copy. Thank you. And can we have on our screens 1D04898, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kijac, on the screen you see this document, and it's before you in hard copy as well. At one point in time, did you give a statement to the members of Mr. Karadzic's Defence team?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we take a look at the last page of this document in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you recognise the signature on this page, Mr. Kijac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whose signature is it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: My own. And the date is the 30th of November, 2013.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to review this statement earlier on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you and I worked through this statement, did we find some abbreviations that were entered erroneously?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes. People weren't paying attention. National security, state security, and so on. And then I didn't even notice myself, when I was giving this statement, that in some cases when there is a reference to the period from the 1st of April, 1992, instead of saying the "National Security Service" in certain paragraphs it said "SDB," which is an abbreviation for the State Security Service. utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So only for the record we would state that this mistake was made in paragraphs 49, 51, 61, and 63. The acronym "SDB" was wrongly used, instead of "SNB," which was the correct abbreviation or acronym for his service from April the 1st, 1992, until the beginning of 1994. And in paragraph 65, acronym "SDB" was wrongly used instead of "RDB," which was the correct abbreviation or acronym for his service in 1994 and 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that the witness will have a look at it and confirm that the testimony you gave a second ago is accurate, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then we can go paragraph by paragraph. Then we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, if the witness would --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you provide the witness with a -- with the information report?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not in English, but I jotted down in conversation with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, would you have a -- perhaps you -- you'll be given a small note on which paragraphs 49, 51, 61, and 63 are mentioned, and would you check whether indeed in those paragraphs the acronyms were wrongly used. And the same is true for paragraph 65. Although there, it is "SDB" what was used where it should be "RDB." Could you check that during the first break, and if -- could -- could a little note be given to the witness with the numbers of the paragraphs. And then we'll hear from you after the break. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apart from these mistakes in terms of the use of acronyms for your service, what about the rest that was recorded in this statement? Was it recorded rightly by the members of Mr. Karadzic's Defence team?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all other microphones please be switched off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is recorded in this statement, to the best of your knowledge, is it correct and truthful?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes. It was done on the basis of the documents that the investigation team of Mr. Karadzic provided to me during preparations and while I was giving this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I were to put the same questions to you today, would you give the same answers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Certainly. Basically the same answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At this moment we maybe should ask for the statement to be MFI'd until the witness checks whether there are the -- use of acronym was correct or incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you already assign a number so that it can be MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D4898 receives Exhibit Number D1292, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Marked for identification. Witness, you said it's based on the documents. This Chamber is interested in your personal knowledge. So therefore, the accuracy or the truthfulness of your statement could not depend on any documents shown to you because what we are interested in is what you can tell us. But may I take it that whatever you have stated as your personal knowledge, that you can attest that that's fully in accordance with the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, since our judiciary system is quite different from the one here, I, as a former employee of the judiciary, went through this statement and I looked at every sentence and every paragraph and tried to confirm everything I said by certain documents. To remember things 25 years later is rather difficult. So this statement is primarily based on the documents that were shown to me, because I now could not exactly say when I was appointed head of the service if I don't see the document involved, or when the service changed its name from the service of national security to the other name, and which exact number of the assembly session it was. But apart from all of this, I will make every effort to speak to the best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that in some respects your recollection was refreshed by looking at the documents but that your answers were all truthful. That's clear now. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I just want to inform Your Honours that there was some problem with the document number of the document in paragraph 51, since the numbers used in this statement were numbers from the Karadzic case, and Mr. Traldi pointed out to me that we used one wrong number in our submission, written submission, 92 ter written motion for this witness. So we just want to tell you that the number noted in this statement is correct. Not the number that we mentioned in our motion. So there is nothing wrong with the statement but only with our motion, and it's 65 ter number from paragraph 51. 01948 should be the correct one and not 09148 as it was mentioned in our motion. Obviously it was just a typo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the P number stands for in that same paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 12 July --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- that's correct -- yeah, that's correct number from Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the P number from Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just for completeness, I wonder if I could ask Mr. Lukic to also put on the record the correct 65 ter in our case. Because the way it came up was the annex to the 92 ter reflected the right 65 ter number in the Mladic case for Karadzic 65 ter 09148 but not for 01948, the document actually used.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. In our case it's 65 ter number 040681.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A lot of numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will read statement summary and I will have questions for this witness afterwards, with your leave. Thank you. Dragan Kijac began his career in state security in 1983 when he was appointed inspector and supervisor for the republican Secretariat of the Interior, State Security Service for Yugoslavia. Before the war in February of 1992, he noticed that Sarajevo police was totally divided along ethnic lines and that within the Sarajevo secretariat there was complete mistrust between personnel of different ethnicities. Worsening of interethnic relations was also caused by the efforts of the SDA to take over all key positions in the Ministry of the Interior. Mr. Kijac witnessed first barricades in Sarajevo and took part in their removal and calming the overall situation. He was also a member of the CSB group that visited the SJBs of Novo Sarajevo and Novi Grad. He saw a greater number of people armed with long-barreled weapons. They were members of the reserve police force who had been activated without his knowledge, although he was the city secretary at that time. His delegation was received in a very hostile fashion and they were not even allowed to address the police officers. It was obvious to him that almost all the police at those stations came from Muslim ethnic group. At the beginning of April 1992, he spent one weekend in Pale area outside Sarajevo. On his way back home, he learned that barricades had been set up again at a number of places in the city, that there was shooting at a number of places, and that no one could enter or leave town. At that moment he decided to remain in Pale area with his family and place himself at the disposal of the MUP of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina which had, in the meantime, been established in Pale. When the war broke out in 1992, Dragan Kijac was appointed chief of the Sarajevo National Security Service Sector of the Ministry of the Interior of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. He later became the head of the State Security Service of Republika Srpska Ministry of the Interior. Mr. Kijac will explain functioning of the State Security Service. Mr. Kijac will explain existence of various groups inside his service like Tajfun, Milos, and others. Dragan Kijac later served as a minister of the interior in the Republika Srpska government and deputy prime minister. That was short statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kijac, now I would like to move on to your statement, paragraphs 40 through 43. You speak about the members of the Tajfun group, then Milos, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the English version page 43 is on page 9 and it is page 16 in B/C/S. [In English] So we need paragraph 43, the next page in B/C/S please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In paragraph 43, you say, from the middle of the paragraph onwards: "Soon afterwards, the members of the group were arrested by the RS MUP." You're referring to the Tajfun group. I quote further on: "I heard of the Milos group for the first time after the arrest of the Tajfun group." Can you explain this to us? Is there any kind of relation between the two, and if so, what is it? The Tajfun group and the Milos group, that is.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: The Tajfun group was created sometime during 1991, the same as the Milos group. But the Tajfun group was created on Mr. Karadzic's order, the president of the republic, because they were made available to him on General Uzelac's suggestion. They were there to inform him about the situation in Croatia in order to try to see a spillover of the war into Bosnia-Herzegovina. These people were mainly from the military structure, and some of them were also close to the civilian security structures. The Milos group was created in a different way, though. The Serbian State Security Service recruited a number of people so as to create a basis for information from Krajina. In addition to the people who were supposed to forward information from Croatia, these people were duty-bound to send information about paramilitary activities in Bosanska Krajina. So the Tajfun group was informing President Karadzic, and the Milos group forwarded their information, given that the man in charge was from the State Security Service, instead of forwarding information to his own service he was forwarding it to the Serbian State Security Service. Later on they were transformed and merged into a single service. We can see that through a number of documents about the Tajfun and Milos group. There came a period where their activities overlapped and they were then merged so as to remain in the field, because by way of my orders and the orders of President Karadzic, they were supposed to have been disbanded at some point.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we next look at 65 ter 19880.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe before we go on, Mr. Lukic, can I just get clarity here. Sir, you're talking of the Milos group forwarded the information to the Serbian State Security Service instead of to the State Security Service. Could you give us the difference between these two institutions? This -- the State Security Service belonged to which government, and the Serbian State Security Service to which government?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps either you or I used the wrong acronym of SDP. They were supposed to have been forwarding information to the SNB at Pale, and instead they were forwarding it to the National Security Service of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before us is a document dated the 29th of January, 1994. It is a dispatch, and we see your name at the bottom. What does this dispatch discuss?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Under the constitution and law, there could not have been two services with the same sphere or activity. In Republika Srpska, there was -- there was a parallel work done by the state national security and the Tajfun. That is why we insisted with President Karadzic to disband the Tajfun, because there were complications in the field. We were often confused with the other group and the other way around. Sometime on the 28th of January, 1994, President Karadzic ordered that this service be terminated. I informed of that all our centres in the field in writing so that they would be made aware that the Tajfun group should no longer exist. And if they did continue working, it would be against the law. I have to stress, though, that we had negotiations with the group on several occasions. The first variant was to terminate the group at the same time incorporating it into the state -- National Security Service. They were offered certain positions in the service, and it took almost a year, the entire process. However, they refused and continued working independently, and then the president ordered that they be disbanded immediately. Irrespective of the president's orders, they did not do so, and later on they were arrested in late 1994, in September or October, I think. The similar story developed -- a similar story developed with the Milos group. In 1992, when I was appointed chief of the National Security Service Sector, I also sent a similar dispatch to our centres informing them that I was appointed to the position. I also forbade any independent communication with the State Security Service of Serbia; i.e., I provided instructions that all information obtained by the centres in the field have to be sent to the SNB centre, and the headquarters was then to decide which documents were to go to the Serbian State Security Service. We did have a law on co-operation with them and we did co-operate in quite a fair way, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was this co-operation with Serbia fair throughout, or were there ups and downs.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: There was many peaks and troughs in the political sense. As far as we were concerned, we tried to do our work professionally. Serbia wanted to know whether the war from Bosnia could spill over into its own territory and whether some regions where Muslims lived could become involved, as well as whether there were any terrorist groups being active. They were interested in any potential plans which would possibly draw Serbia into the war. They were also interested in not seeing the war spill over into Croatia the same way it came from Croatia into Bosnia. So if I can say so, they were interested in capital information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's time for break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we had a late start --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Or I should to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's continue for ten minutes. We have a little bit less time this morning anyhow than --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would just offer this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 19880 receives Exhibit Number D1293, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1293 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us who was the personnel of Tajfun and Milos, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: I can't say. I can't mention any names today. I do know that the Tajfun was headed by Branko Ratic and Predrag Radulovic headed the Milos group. He had previously worked in the security services centre in Banja Luka. In terms of members, I don't remember any names.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's look at another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need 1D06122.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before we see it on the screen, let me ask you this: What did you do when you found out about the Milos group?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Given that the Tajfun group had been arrested by that time and some sort of co-operation was already established, then we realised that, inter alia, they received some of their information from the National Security Service; i.e., that in the National Security Service Sector in Banja Luka, there are people linked with the group. When we found out that the group was forwarding its information to Belgrade without us knowing, we terminated the employment of Predrag Radulovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The document before us has not been translated, and I will read it out slowly so that everyone is aware of what it's about. It is a document of the state security centre in Banja Luka, dated the 4th of November, 1994. The reference is to Predrag Radulovic, a mutual agreement on termination of employment. It is signed by the State Security Sector chief, Kesic, Nedeljko. How come there was a consensual termination of Radulovic's employment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Standard practice in services such as ours is not to terminate employment unilaterally. Usually it is a matter of consent. Had we decided to do it unilaterally, there would have been a disciplinary procedure instituted. We would need to submit a criminal report for unauthorised disclosure of information that is state secret, irrespective of whether he co-operated with a friendly or enemy security service. In order to deal with it as painlessly as possible, we sat him down and agreed with him that it would be best if his employment were to be terminated, if he initiated the termination so that it would be consensual under the law. It was not the first case of that nature. I worked many years in the State Security Services and most such instances were dealt with through the use of this instrument, even when the situations concerned involved criminal offences.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would ask for this document to be MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D06122 receives Exhibit Number D1294, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just ask that Mr. Lukic provide provenance information as to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kijac, do you know how this document came into the possession of the Defence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: I don't know. I can see that the document is original. It is signed by the chief of centre. It comes from the State Security Sector in Banja Luka. I see the date. But I can't say how somebody could obtain this document. It must be somewhere in the personal file of Mr. Radulovic. This document is somewhere in the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And we inherited it from Karadzic team, so they obtained the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm satisfied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Therefore, of course, if the witness doesn't know it, it's -- I mean, you could have directly answered the question that: We got it from the Karadzic Defence. Because that's apparently --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I thought maybe he gave it to Karadzic Defence, that's why I didn't want to lead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the reason why, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we scroll the document down, please. Let's see the full page. Is it usual, Mr. Kijac, that a document of this nature would not have a -- have an official date stamp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am surprised to see that there is no stamp. But in terms of a filing number, we see it there. We see the date. Maybe this is one of the copies in existence. I can't say. But I suppose this document would have been received in my office with a stamp. It is possible that this copy may have been kept in the centre in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But you just said in answer to Mr. Lukic's question that it is -- that this is an original. Now you're saying it's a copy.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose that an original was sent to me. This was proposed by his chief of centre, his immediate superior, and the document was sent to Pale. Mr. Nedeljko Kesic was not the person who could terminate his employment. I was in charge of doing that as the head of sector. And you can see that in the attachment to this document, there was a request by Mr. Radulovic. I was the one to terminate his employment. Kesic could not do that. The legal service was in -- at the headquarters in Pale. They would draft the document and I signed it. I suppose this copy is from his personal file where a copy remains and the original was sent to Pale. That would be my explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm getting a little confused, sir. You earlier said that you didn't know where this document comes from. Now you're saying it must have been sent to you because you were the one who could terminate that employment. Does this document refresh your memory as to whether you did or did not receive a request to terminate this employment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We did terminate his employment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So -- so you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- but I don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So can you then tell us the origin of this document, the provenance of this document? Apart from saying that you saw it in the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The source is the Banja Luka centre of the State Security Service. It has it -- their register number. I probably received an original with a stamp. I need not have had it in my hands personally because it is sent to the legal affairs department, and the head of that department also has the right to sign such documents in my absence when it comes to termination of employment. In my view, this is an authentic document without a stamp. In all likelihood, this document was sent to the headquarters of the service and in that case it did have a stamp and signature. I don't know if you are with me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I am not with you because you're confusing me further. Earlier you said you received this and it does refresh your memory, you terminated this. Now you're saying you may not have received it because it was sent to the centre. I'm not quite sure whether you, as you stand here, did or did not receive this document. Because now you're telling -- you're saying that it came into the centre, you may not have read it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, Your Honour, initiating employment and terminating employment comes from lower-ranking organisational units to the top of the service; i.e., any proposal on initiation or termination comes from the CSBs such as the Banja Luka one in this case. It could have been Doboj, Bijeljina, Sarajevo or Herzegovina, that is to say, Trebinje. All of that comes to the headquarters of the service and there the service drafts decisions. I can't say with any certainty whether I saw this document. It does refresh my recollection in the sense that I am aware that his employment was terminated and that he was employed later on with the service. But this piece of paper does not tell me anything else, anything other than that specifically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then I give up. I've got several answers to the same question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, it looks as if you're reconstructing what may have happened, whereas Judge Moloto is primarily interested in what you remember that you personally did at the time or saw at the time. Mr. Traldi, you're already for a while on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to raise, and I see we're at the time Your Honour had identified for the break, but just to say that we'd checked our records as -- I noticed after I stood up that there is an ERN on it and we'd received it from CSB Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's then ... Mr. Lukic, the witness referred to an attachment. I've not seen any attachment at this moment. Is that -- is it there or --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says on the bottom --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- of the left corner, attachment 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But do you know the attachment?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It must be his request, Radulovic's request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not with this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have it --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We do not have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You do not have it, but the witness apparently knew what it was about because that's what he said. We'll take a break first. Witness, would you please take your statement with you and check the paragraphs whether they actually indicate what the paragraphs were that underwent the changes in the acronyms. Has the witness been provided with -- yes, the witness has been provided with the numbers of the paragraphs as well. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. We can take a break. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at five minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom. I perhaps could already briefly deal with a short matter. On the 8th of October of this year, the Defence has filed a motion to, inter alia, add Dragan Vujicic to its 65 ter witness list. Given that the Prosecution indicated on the record on the 6th of October that they did not object to this witness providing his evidence via videolink -- video-conference link, the Chamber understands that the Prosecution also has no objections to the Defence adding this witness to its Rule 65 ter list. We consider this to be implied. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Precisely, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the Chamber hereby grants the Defence's request to add Witness Dragan Vujicic to its Rule 65 ter witness list with written reasons to follow in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It may even be that we provide the reasons orally, so the announcement that these will be written reasons should not be taken too strictly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Welcome back, Mr. Kijac. Could you confirm that the corrections as far as the acronyms are concerned should be made in paragraphs 49, 51, 61, and 63, where instead of "SDB" we should read "SNB"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In paragraph 49, line 1, instead of "SDB," it should read "RDB." Further on in the same paragraph: "Therefore, I was surprised to hear this information of the SNB." It should be "RDB." Your Honour, this service from 1992 was called SNB, but from 1994 onwards it was the State Security Sector, and this is probably why this happened. I see in paragraph 51 as well. The first one where it says "SDB" it should be "RDB," and probably it was not noticed because, say, 61, RDB/ -- also RDB, SDB, so at one point it was the National Security Service and later on it was the State Security Sector. Also in paragraph 63. And in paragraph 65, the last paragraph --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all other microphones please be switched off. We can barely hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I was speaking too fast. I'm not sure that you can follow everything that I've been saying. So the official name of the service from the 1st of April -- rather, the 4th of April, 1992, was the National Security Service. And from 1994, it was the Sector for State Security.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then paragraph 65?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 65, this very last sentence pertains to the period of 1995, so the "SDB" in the last sentence is wrong. It should be "RDB." The last sentence in paragraph 65.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's hereby corrected. Madam Registrar, could you remind me what number was assigned when the statement was MFI'd so that it can be admitted? I think it's D1292. D1292 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just another clarification, please. After the 1st of April, 1992, up until the end of the war, was there ever a service within MUP that would have the acronym SDB?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: No. So from 1992 the official name of the service was the National Security Service, and then from 1994, I think it was the 36th Assembly Session, the law was changed, and then the National Security Service was renamed the State Security Sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We had a document before us, D1294. That's the MFI number. There is no translation. However, I'm going to ask you only whether you recognise the signature on this document.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: By all means. It is Nedeljko Kesic, the head of the RDB centre in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm sorry I keep jumping from one thing to another now, but we have to go back to your statement again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D1292. We need pages 8 in English and 13 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need paragraph 35 of your statement. This is what you say here -- actually, you speak about being appointed acting undersecretary for the SNB in the MUP of the Serbian Republic of BH, and further down you say in the second half of this paragraph: "I informed the organisational units of the service that I was taking over the post of undersecretary and in the same document prohibited the hiring of new staff without the approval of the responsible supervisor and direct contacts with services outside the RS, which had been common practice before my appointment." You told us about the problems with Tajfun, Milos. Was there any other group?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: We did not know about groups, but there were certain individuals. How do I put this? They operated in a similar way, in a way similar to the Milos group. At that time, we did not know that much about it. It was only later, when documents became available and when the many years went by, I saw that there were groups -- or, no, rather, individuals who had contacted other services and provided certain information to other services. I can say that often this was misinformation based on one-sided assessments, and that is why we insisted that the communication with the Serbian service should be at the level of the two services, not organisational units on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The transcript does not reflect whether you said that there was direct communication between operatives themselves?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes, I said at the level of operatives who were contacted by operatives of other services and then through them they gave certain information about the situation in Republika Srpska. But I'm saying that very often this was unverified, one-sided information that individuals could not view in their entirety because they were at a lower rank in the service.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now let us take a look at another document that hasn't been translated. I think that it's the last untranslated document that we will be looking at, 1D06123.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see that this is a document of the basic court in Teslic. The document was written on the 12th of October, 2001. It is being sent to the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska in Banja Luka. And the subject is the return of court file number KI35/02. The first paragraph says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it 02 or 92?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Or 92. 92. It is I think 02. No, no, it is 92. Sorry. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the Chamber will consider whether it's 02 or 92. If you look at the other 0s at the top of the document, you see that it's inconsistently used. Apparently sometimes there is a real 0 which we find at the very top of the document, whereas for the date, for example, small Os are used. And whether this is 92 or --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is a little tail but very hardly visible on the first number as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If I might assist, Your Honours, the KI number also appears in the second full paragraph of the text as well as the last full paragraph, and in both of those the tail Mr. Lukic is describing is a little bit clearer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I tend -- of course, I see it now for the first time, but KI35-92 appears several times clearly visible. So there isn't -- there is at least some reason to assume that that's also what is meant in the title line. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this is what is written in the first paragraph, and I quote: "Criminal proceedings are underway before this court registered under number K52/01 against the accused Predrag Radulovic from Banja Luka." In the third paragraph, it says that: "For reasons unknown and unexplainable, the file was sent to the Ministry of the Judiciary of Republika Srpska to the assistant minister, Goran Neskovic." At any rate, it says that this file has been lost. There has been no trace of it. Do you know anything about this, about the criminal proceedings against Predrag Radulovic that was taking place during those years?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: If I can give the right kind of comment with regard to this. First of all, against Radulovic there is this number K52/01. That's 2001. So I was not even in the Ministry of Republika Srpska, and I wasn't even in Republika Srpska itself. I had already moved to Belgrade. And then further down there is another number, KI35/92. So that's completely different and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you're not invited to comment on the document. The question was whether you know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Regarding the proceedings against Radulovic, no. I was not in the Ministry of the Interior at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you, did you see this document before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I just saw it during preparations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You haven't seen it when you gave your statement to the Karadzic Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not this document. Well, I could not familiarise myself with this document because this document bears the date of the 12th of October, 2001. In 1990 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you've answered my question, that you haven't seen it at the time. Of course, Mr. Lukic, the Chamber wonders what it exactly -- the exact evidentiary purpose of it -- it is at this moment where the witness can't say anything about it, but please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Although there is no translation, the witness does not know anything about the document, but still we'll -- still we would offer it into evidence. Still it has -- it can provide us with contextual base in regard of Radulovic, Predrag.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I don't know what his role is in -- in the Defence case, but it's indeed --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness has said something about it. Any objections, Mr. Traldi?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course to be MFI'd first, but as far as the subject matter is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No objections to it be being MFI'd as a contextual document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, could you assign a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D06123 receives Exhibit Number D1295.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next could we actually go back to Mr. Kijac's statement on the screen, and it is D1292.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the document, I think there was something about the transcript. You said that Mr. Radulovic had his employment terminated in a consensual way with the State Security Service and that later on he was again employed, but we are missing where. Was he re-employed in the National Security Service? No --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness kindly repeat his answer. There was an overlap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer, Witness, because there was an overlap.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. After his termination was -- employment was terminated with the State Security Sector, Mr. Radulovic was re-employed in the public security service later on; although, I don't know what his job was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We are with your statement here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need page 7 in English and 12 in B/C/S, paragraph 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the paragraph, you explain the chain a piece of information covers from its source to the end user. In the last sentence, you say, when speaking about a field operative compiling an Official Note, that he needs to specify the sources of his knowledge and verify the accuracy of information: "He forwards the Official Note to his immediate superior, the chief of the branch station."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In light of this could we look at another document. It is a Prosecution exhibit, P06890. Before us is an Official Note. In order to be able to follow what we are talking about -- in any case, we do need the English version on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First of all, a question about the rules of service. What kind of rules were they? Were they new or inherited rules? Which rules did the service of national security rely on after the 1st of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: They were inherited rules. We used the same rules that were in place in Sarajevo at the time. We had no time to draft new rules. The new rules were only introduced sometime in 1993 or 1994. We had no new rules. We relied on the ones used in the joint State Security Service of Bosnia and Herzegovina. They were identical. Only later, as time passed by, requests from the field showed a distinct need for it because new offices, new administrations were created, but that happened later as of 1993 or 1994, as I said. I would like us to briefly look at a Defence document so as to be able to comment upon this one before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For a short while, could we have D00649.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have an Official Note here. Tell us whether it contains standard elements required by the rules in order to be part of an Official Note. And if so, please tell us what they are.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes. There must be a heading. There must be a number, a date. There should be the name of an operative or his code of the person drafting it. They also need to specify the course of information, because it can be fully reliable, reliable, unverified, unreliable, and so on, so they need to specify whether the information they received was reliable. Of course, they also had to sign and suggest measures to be taken in order to further verify the information referred to. This is what an SNB document should look like. We can see this one was drafted as per the rules and according to the guide-lines issued on providing information within the service.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Without referring to the name of the person who signed this document, do you nevertheless know him as your operative?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now go back to the previous document, P06890. Official Note. Let us look at the last page in both versions. All it says at the bottom is that it was drafted in two copies and "Milos" is in the signature block. Let us now go back to the first page, please. Let me put my question now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to you, does this document contain all the elements necessary as envisaged by your service?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You have read the document; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes, I had the occasion to read it twice. I also received it from you some two days ago. I read it. One can immediately say that it does not correspond to the template of documents produced either by the sector or state of national security, at least at the time when I was at its helm.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you yourself said, we see that the date, among other things, is missing, but we can tell something from the contents. We see that we don't know when the event referred to actually took place. Is this customary and permissible in the way your service operated?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: No. The first sentence should have contained a date, say: On this or that date through contacts with a large number of sources and so on. Whoever received the document cannot guess whether it was drafted two months ago, half a year ago, or a year ago. Every document should begin with a date: We spoke to this or that person on this or that date. There is no need to mention names but at least the initials should be there. And based on that, we know the time. It doesn't need to mean that it was done the same day. For example, a conversation takes place today and the document can be produced three days later. That is why in the heading we need to have the date the document was created and sent to those higher up in the chain.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You did touch upon something that I want to explore further. Did you find in the document at least a year that this refers to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Not the way I see it. There is no date in the document whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about this document personally about what is described here or do you have any knowledge about the events described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we don't need a witness to tell us that there is no year in the document. This Chamber can read and can see whether there is a reference to a year or not. This witness apparently doesn't know anything about this document itself. He has explained to us that this is not the usual way of drafting these kind of documents, but it doesn't go that much further. And I do understand that this document I think which was initially -- well, not formally introduced but at least dealt with by the Defence and then more or less taken over by the Prosecution, that -- let's try to elicit from the witness what he can tell us from his personal knowledge and observations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: His personal knowledge in regard of this particular document is obviously zero, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- he knows the rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fine. Okay. Yes. Then ask him about the rules. You have done that. He's told us now that -- but now you are asking him whether a date appears on a document on which he has no knowledge whatsoever, and again we can read.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But there is no mentioning of the year even. There is nothing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I mean, we can see that. I mean, don't ask the witness that there is no year there because we -- we can see that with our own eyes. But let's leave it to that and please focus on what the witness could further tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In documents such as this one, Mr. Kijac, should one determine whether the information provided is verified or unverified?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: It should say whether they were verified or not. If someone says that the information was verified, it means that it was done by technical means, i.e., a dispatch was intercepted, for example. So if a piece of information is very reliable, it relies on technical source. Reliable sources, however, is a combination of operative work with people whom we have been co-operating for a number of years and we know they provide accurate data. The third classification is unverified information, meaning that at that point in time we are unable to do so. In other words, certain measures need to be taken to make them either accepted or rejected.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The document was signed with "Milos." The operative who drafted it, did they determine whether the information was verified or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: No, I can't see it in the document. If I may, I can offer a comment. Some things are referred to in the document that have nothing to do with our service whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll go one step at a time. We see that the source were people, as we can see in the first paragraph. And that it -- the information was obtained through a number of sources and discussions with some officials in the Teslic SJB. What needed to be done after this paragraph in the document in your view?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: If such an Official Note received this sector, instructions would be provided to conduct official interviews with these people and to forward that information to us in order to be able to gauge how serious the information actually is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see from this whether such statements were taken from these people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: I didn't see that, nor did I see any such measures being suggested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, again you're asking the witness to tell us what he reads in the document. As I said before, we can read it ourselves. So if --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Should I then lead him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- nothing is said about --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Should I then lead him, tell him what's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- in the document and then ask him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I do that way, then you will say "you are leading the witness."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, you just should leave it to the Chamber to read this documents and not ask the witness to do that for us where he has no further knowledge about the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, then I asked him further whether he -- that should be done --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, Mr. Lukic, please -- please follow my guidance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The member of your service who drafted your service -- this document, was he supposed to notify his superiors of this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see from the document whether he did inform them about the contents of this information or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: No, we can't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you're not following my guidance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you cannot see from a document is not in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Therefore we don't need a witness for that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the exhibit -- Prosecution exhibit. We want to show what kind of exhibit we have in front of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you know the history of this document. We excluded initially a paragraph from a statement and then it was due to the Defence's actions later that finally, I think it was paragraph 133 of Mr. Radulovic's statement that -- which we had excluded, that you yourself triggered that it was back in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour. But we [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- we have to challenge the document. We did not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The only thing I'm asking you, and please follow us, is that don't ask this witness what you can read from the document or not because that's what we can do ourselves. And you repeatedly have done it and you should stop doing it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Were you supposed to see this paper, Mr. Kijac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe the translation hadn't finished. I do apologise. Have you seen this document? Did you see it while you worked at the National Security Service?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: No, I first saw it a few days ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you supposed to see it? What do you think?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, if it was written by the service, it certainly should have reached the top echelons of the service by way of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Had you seen it, what would you have done?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Well, probably we would have asked for statements to be taken from these people, because that's the only way in which we could confirm or deny these allegations. That is to say, take statements from these people and on that basis compile information for the leadership.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, General Mladic and the president of the municipality, can they issue orders to the police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: No. There is a chain of command in the police that goes up to the minister of the interior, and outside that no one can interfere in the interior regardless of the position a person may hold. Even if that person is the commander of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On that document in this page on paragraph 3, in the English version it is line 4 in paragraph 3, it says that the management of the public security service requested some suggestions and opinions of employees of the Banja Luka SNB concerning the performance of tasks issued to them. The National Security Service, can it provide suggestions and opinions to the public security service?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: These are two completely autonomous services, that is to say, the state security and the public security. Every one of them has its particular purview according to law. We are an intelligence agency and we collect information. We cannot direct the work of the public security service. We can provide certain suggestions. And when a particular case has something to do with our work - that is to say, when we can give some suggestions to the public security service to warn us about a certain person crossing the border, for instance - we send a dispatch and we say: If XY crosses the border, tell us about it, stop him, and so on and so forth. And now as for this leadership, they have leaders of their own. You cannot explain to the chief of a station what his job is when it is the law that stipulates what his job is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You told us that the document does not show what measures were supposed to be taken by the author of this document. Were measures supposed to be proposed as to the measures that should be taken?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, no speaking aloud. Last warning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does one have to know who compiled the document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: According to the instructions regarding our information that we had, yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If a code were used as a signature, how is that code determined?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: On the basis of the sector involved; that is to say, the sector knows who the operative involved is at every point in time. So some centres had codes. For example, A4 was for example the code-name for a certain individual. I have that list and the centre has that list, and if I'm interested in seeing who it was that wrote this up and if this information draws your attention, then you can see what the name is of the person who wrote that. So at any point when I was interested in a particular paper, I could see who was the operative who wrote that particular paper. However, I think that Banja Luka then did not have code-names. I think it was only Sarajevo at first. I'm talking about, say, 1992. I think that Banja Luka never had code-names for their personnel. They used their names and surnames to sign documents. So one can see exactly who it was that created the document and also who typed the document and, of course, who signed it so that it could be sent to the top echelons of the service later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This code-name Milos, do you think that it was assigned by the service or how come somebody signs a document by "Milos"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Probably this was a code-name that had been agreed earlier on the basis of their contacts with another service. I find it unknown. In our terminology we did not have a group named Milos or a pseudonym by the name of Milos. If this were 1993, I would say that this was not our document. Also, if it was 1992. Milos is totally unknown. It's only later the group Milos was revealed, and then it became a bit clearer. But, I mean, I didn't even see this paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have any views of your own as to what kind of document this is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Well, to be honest, this document is very, very - how do I put this? - written in a very lopsided way. There are certain things that are mentioned here. Certain things that - how do I put this? - are not grounded in what the author offered through this text. Let's move on to the next page, for instance, and then I can tell you about that. Could I have the next page of the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please, could we move to the second page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see how this is. Milanovic, Major, Vukasin, Radic, insisted. Insisted with who? And then it says that that is in the media that the people in Srpska are leaving certain municipalities. Then one would have to give the example of these municipalities straight away. And towards the end in the last paragraph it says: "All of this causes revolt on the part of a large number of Serbs" -- Oh, sorry, I really made a mistake here. Sorry about that. "... that are showing interest to move out of the territory of municipalities." He should have said this and that municipality so that people would know exactly what this is all about. Or, for instance, that this is in the media. Then there should be information as to which media, what article, who wrote the article, in which period. So this is really very -- I mean, we have a saying that goes: Nothing but the best about the dead. But I must say that Mr. Radulovic was totally illiterate for this kind of work. I have to say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I think we have heard enough opinion evidence now from a witness of fact. Would you please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that before we had the opportunity to listen to people who have experience in that field to give their opinion, although they are not experts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the reason why I didn't stop you earlier. That's the reason why at this moment I say we moved from the knowledge of the witness about how the system works to his personal interpretation now and that the document in no way meets what this witness would have expected from such a document. That is abundantly clear at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will move on then. Again we need D1992, your -- the statement of Mr. Kijac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I think we are close to your one and a half-hour, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that -- but half an hour before the break and close to one hour after the break. Please proceed. It was even more than half an hour before the break. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So in paragraph 4 of your statement, you said that on the 6th of April, 1992, you were appointed chief of the National Security Service sector. And in paragraph 26, you said where it was that you had your departments. That was in Ilidza, Ilijas, Pale, and Sokolac. And the headquarters of the service was in Lukavica. What about Trnovo, was there a department there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: No, no, there wasn't a department in Trnovo. That is to say, when I was appointed chief of the Sarajevo SSNB, we had four departments: Ilidza, Ilijas, Pale, and Sokolac. And the headquarters of the sector was in Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us see P06888 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I showed you this information, this report on the operation and activities of the TO command Main Staff and the commanding personnel of the Trnovo armed forces. Let us look at the last page of this document. It just says: State Security Service Trnovo, by way of a signature. So this kind of signature, department of SDB Trnovo, could that have existed if somebody from your service had written this up?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm not going to put any questions to you because we can see it from the document itself. We don't see who it was that compiled this document. Should we be able to see -- if somebody from your service had written this up, should we see who the author was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes, we would have to see who the author was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It can be seen that one cannot see who this document is being sent to. Is that the way it was supposed to be? Were we supposed to be able to see who this document is being sent to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Certainly. Because, in fact, had our service written this document, it would have had to reach my desk. It's May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: June.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes, but I was chief of sector at that point in time. But we never received a single document from Trnovo and we could not get to Trnovo at that point in time. Our department was in Ilidza, and there was no communication with Trnovo because of the sniping and because of the situation there. And as for these documents that you showed me the other day, there is a reference to a Muslim barricade; that is to say, that the road is inaccessible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever have any operatives in Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: I don't think so. I think that we dealt with Trnovo only when there was fighting for Trnovo. That is to say, in a period that came after this one. Since that road was very important to us because of the link with Herzegovina from Foca onwards, at that point in time, we would sent an operative who is familiar with the ground. Usually it was people like that who were sent. We saw a signature a moment ago, (redacted) (redacted) and he usually went there in order to be able to follow the combat activities taking place in the area of Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does this document look like something that (redacted) would have written up?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: No, there is no chance of us having created this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From the document we cannot see when it was created. Was one supposed to say when this kind of document was created if it's created by your service?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: If it were our document and if it were the document of the Muslim service at the time, if I can call it that way, there has to be a letterhead, there has to be a signature, there has to be a date. There has to be everything that we talked about in relation to the previous document. Every document has to contain certain elements and that's the way it's supposed to be. And the document that you showed me from the area of Ilidza is an example of that. So you can see that it's the Ministry of the Interior, the sector of the National Security Service Sarajevo, the number, the date, and so on and so forth. Each and every document should have these elements.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this document, we also cannot see which operative compiled this information. Is that indispensable for this kind of document, otherwise?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see a document of the National Security Service that would speak about expulsions and killings of Muslims and others?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I mean, where that is being advocated?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: No, no. Sometimes there would be mention of crimes committed on ethnic grounds, and then somebody provided information that there was a murder or two murders in a certain place, but we did not deal with that. Somebody could have written a document like that, and such a document could have reached me. However, we had an inter-sector agreement: Murder is murder. So it is the public security sector that dealt with this even during the times of war. We were not in charge of that. We did not have personnel that was capable of dealing with such cases. So we could have received a dispatch from the centre that somebody had killed somebody else and that this caused anxiety and so on and so forth, and this kind of thing did happen. You know, it -- there is a war going on and somebody would, say, come back and create a problem of this kind. But put in this way, the way that you have asked me, no. Again, I have to point out one more thing if you allow me. I never attended a meeting -- and I attended many meetings of the state and military leadership. I never attended a single meeting where there were any kind of references like what you said to me just a second ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You had the opportunity of reading the entire document. And now at the end, the 29th of May, 1992, the date at the end of this document, can you see here who it is that is actually speaking?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: No. That's interesting. This document, in terms of dates, everybody knows who was saying what, and then all of a sudden at a joint meeting such and such a conclusion was reached. So there are two such documents, I think, similar ones, but the conclusions do not match. And there is always these two staffs, if I can put it, the Crisis Staff and this one. They function along parallel lines. And then you have two different conclusions. In essence they are the same, but they are not the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Briefly, P06889. Could we take a look at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are at the time for a break, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How much time do I have?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think some seven or eight minutes left. If you would like to take that now before the break, but then perhaps you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It may be better to reorganise. I can -- easier to cut down the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There are not many left, then. Let's take a break now and then I expect you to finish in -- well, let's say ten minutes after the break. The witness may follow the usher. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at -- yes, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, could we briefly go into private session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We take a break and will resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we have P06889 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before us is a document similar to the previous one. It is a report on the activity and work of the Trnovo SDS Municipal Board from 1 January to 31 May 1992. Let us look at the last page. Again in the signature block, we see the Trnovo SDB department. You told us that at the time in your service no such abbreviation or organisation existed. We determined that it should be visible who created this document, like the previous one as well. With the previous document, we also determined that it should be clear who the document is sent to and that in that document as well as this one we cannot see that. We also established in the previous document as can be seen in this one that no date is present --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you haven't established anything. You have elicited evidence from a witness, which is different from determining or establishing. Whatever the witness said about what we need in such kind of a document is on the record. Whether it's in here, yes or no, we can read that. So whether it's the same as the previous one, the Chamber will consider that. Could you please put a question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the operative in question have to make clear who drafted the document? The person who wrote the document, if it was an operative from your service, did they need to make it clear who drafted the document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes, just like everything I said with regard to the first document. The two documents seem identical in terms of the things they lack, procedurally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, do you have any personal knowledge about this document apart from having seen it a couple of days ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does everything you said earlier about what a report should contain, would that apply to this report as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If this had been drafted by a member of your service, would this document have arrived at your desk in May or June 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes. At the time, I was the chief of the National Security Sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see the document at the time or did you see it only when I showed it to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: I saw it a couple of days ago when you showed it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your view -- well, in the penultimate line we read that: "The aggression on Trnovo and the surrounding Muslim villages started at 0830 in the morning of 31 May 1992." Did the Serb side in its own documents describe its own actions as "aggression," if you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: No. It's a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me just ask you this. Do you have an opinion, having read the document, as to this: In a previous part of the document -- so let me restart that. In the previous part of the document, can we see who is reporting about what? There are two dates, the 29th and the 30th of May.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Well, we can see that there were some briefings at meetings. But in the conclusions, we cannot see who stated what. There is just a statement. It is correct that in both documents people were being said as having said this or that on this or that date. And in the last paragraph here, as in the previous document, we cannot see what position they expressed and who said what personally. There is no discussion referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Lukic, the Chamber can read. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As an employee and chief of the National Security Service, what would be your opinion of this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't know how to characterise it other than to say that it is not valid. Documents such as this one are not valid in the service. They need to contain all the elements we discussed. Only such documents are considered valid. In one of the paragraphs of my statement, I mention that we issued instructions on providing information and how they had to be used to provide information accurately. This is definitely not a document of the service I headed. This document may have been created sometime in June, when I was already in the position of the Sarajevo sector chief for sometime. I never received it. I see it for the first time, and I'm not aware of issues in Trnovo. It is not our document. I don't know what else to say.
