I think the National Security Service of Bosnia and Herzegovina, too, had to rely on a heading and all the elements we talked about because it was all happening at the same time. There was only a change of name. They had the State Security Service and we had the National Security Service. I can't even presume or suppose whose document this might be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I have one follow-up question for the witness. A minute ago you were asked by Mr. Lukic if the Serb side in its own documents described its own actions as "aggression." Your answer was: "No. It's a fact." I don't fully understand your answer. What do you mean by "it is a fact"? What is a fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it is fact that VRS operations were not called "aggression" in certain areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the witness has opined quite a bit though being a witness of fact, but could you please conclude in one or two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My last question, Mr. Kijac. In any of the documents you saw that came from your service, did you ever see as an operation on the Serb side being called "aggression"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat because there was an overlap?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I wasn't following the B/C/S channel. So in any document you saw as a document created by the Serb side, be it your service or the army, did the Serb side, was it ever marked as "aggressor" in its own documents?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: No. I think I said clearly that it was not possible --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, exactly the same question was put by you on page 51, line 21: "Did the Serb side in its own documents describe," et cetera. Then even in order to fully understand the answer, Judge Fluegge asked for -- to know for sure that he understood the answer well. Now you're asking the same. I asked you to conclude in one or two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, I just repeated this one because you said that the witness gave his opinion. If you see something or do not see something, it's not an opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was on the question you put after that: Could you give us your views on the document that was, and then we got a lengthy answer, all opinion evidence, hardly anything about facts. So that's a different matter. But there is no need to put a question again to a witness in order to correct me. Any further question, or have you done?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you discussed this document and provided your opinion, what was the basis for it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, there was an overlap again. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you discussed this document and provided your opinion, what was the basis of your opinion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm going to stop you now. I mean, if you elicit opinion evidence and then ask the witness on what it is based, then you should have asked him about the facts which may have underlied his opinion. But if I say something about eliciting opinion evidence, which we let go through quite a while, then to say on what it was based, you should have asked that before, perhaps even instead of, asking for opinion evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, this question --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- is not further allowed. Have you any other question of fact --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I enumerated the facts, then you stopped me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, this is not a debate. This was a ruling. Any other question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your ruling does not allow me to finish this correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Moloto will ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you have asked the witness to give the basis for his opinion. He told us the basis is the fact that there are no reference numbers, there is no signature, it is not addressed to anybody, it is not signed by anybody, and all the other things. That is the basis for his opinion. What more do you want from him?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: His experience as a head of the sector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But he has told us his experience. He has told us several times why he says this is not a document from his sector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He put it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now you're asking him for the -- the same --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If that pleases the Court, I do not have any more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Of course that was the basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just to thank Mr. Kijac for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's of course appreciated. Mr. Kijac, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Traldi. You'll find Mr. Traldi to your right. Mr. Traldi is counsel for the Prosecution, but is there -- Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The translation is still going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kijac, I just wanted to thank you for having answered our questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kijac, I think you may have heard my introduction of Mr. Traldi who will now cross-examine you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you testified in the Karadzic case; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And is it your position that you told the truth in that testimony?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 17058A.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, what you see on the left side of the screen in B/C/S, that's your appointment as SNB undersecretary signed by Minister Stanisic; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And he was your immediate superior until he was replaced and then the next minister, Minister Adzic, was your immediate superior; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the minister's superior was the president of the republic, Radovan Karadzic; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, your deputy was Dragisa Mihic; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And as head of the SNB, you would have received reports from all of the five regional SNBs; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And as head of the SNB, you were also a member of the ministers' collegium; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And so you also received information at collegium meetings about what was going on in regional CSBs and in their subordinate SJBs; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: There is something that we need to understand. The collegium comprised some 20 people. There was only one representative from the National Security Service. Some of the briefings by my colleagues were not of my concern. The law states that the service is a separate service within the ministry with the chief at its helm. If we are discussing the ministers' collegium, there were some 20 people there, and only rarely did the service take part in discussions. Very rarely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And when you attended meetings of that collegium, you would receive information provided by the other members of the collegium about events in their areas of responsibility; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: There were discussions, but I did not receive any information from them. We did not receive, for example, information from the State Security Service. I'm sorry, the public security service. We did provide some information to the public security service, but there was no information coming our way. We were in communication, there was correspondence, but they were not duty-bound to provide information to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I understand that, sir. At the moment, I'm not asking about what they were duty-bound to provide. I'm asking as a factual matter: At these collegium meetings when you attended them, the other members would speak about, would discuss events in their areas of responsibility, and as a result of them mentioning them, you would become informed about them. That's true, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: No. Public law and order were not of my interest. I was present physically, but I may have been absent psychologically. You need to understand that we were a completely independent service. In 1995, our system became so independent that we were no longer under the minister. Such was the situation under the law. In terms of how we conducted ourselves, we were an independent service. We were only duty-bound to inform the minister of our --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, could I stop you there. Would you please focus to answer on the question. I think you may have answered it already, that you said: Although I may have been present and although information was perhaps provided, I may not have listened to it. That's apparently your answer and that answers the question, so we are now waiting for the next question. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Before I do, I'll tender the document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you do, Mr. Traldi, can I just ask a clarification from you. I see the English version doesn't have the name of the person and the status of the person who signed it. Is -- and the fact that they were originally stamped.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm told it should be on the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar informs me that we have only one page in English, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: My -- then I will withdraw what I was told and will check the upload. I'd just ask that it be marked at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could -- Madam Registrar, the number under which this document would be marked for identification will be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 17058A receives Exhibit Number P7576, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7576 is marked for identification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 02382.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, while it comes up, as head of the SNB, you co-operated with the VRS and the State Security Services of Serbia, Montenegro, and the RSK; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In that context, I'm going to read you a description of the SNB's co-operation with some of those institutions that you provided at the 34th Session of the Republika Srpska Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And can we have page 215 in the English and 234 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In the English, we're at the beginning of your remarks, in the B/C/S on the second page of them. And at the bottom of the page in the English and in the middle of the long paragraph in the B/C/S, you begin to give a long description of the SNB. And you say: "Among other things, in accordance with its duties, SNB is on a daily basis exchanging security-related information with, first of all, the security service of RS army, then with Republic Serbia, Montenegro, and SRK." That's correct, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in the VRS your contacts would have been with General Tolimir; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes. And Colonel Petar Salapura.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And with the Republic of Serbia, your contacts would have been with Jovica Stanisic and his subordinate administrations in the DB; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Basically with the top of the service.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So by that do you mean to refer to Mr. Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you would have also had contact with his subordinate, Frenki Simatovic; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Very rarely. I mean, we know each other. But this happened very rarely. I mean, do you understand this? We had correspondence and it was mainly directed to the head of the service and later on the departments, so I did not have any particular contact with Mr. Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Mr. Simatovic, with whom you rarely had contact, he was the head of the Second Administration in DB Serbia; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: I don't know what their organisation was like, but I did not co-operate with administrations. In our Second Administration, he had his opposite number. If Mr. Simatovic was head of the Second Administration, then the head of the Second Administration could have had contact with him. So if I maintain contact, I maintained contact with Mr. Stanisic. You see? Now you can say to me that I maintained contact with the Seventh, Sixth Administration, and so on. That was not my job. From the moment when I became head of the service, it is appropriate for the head of service to speak to his opposite number, the head of the other service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the simple question was whether Mr. Simatovic, with whom you rarely had contact, whether he was the head of the Second Administration in the DB of Serbia. Was he, was he not, or don't you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Believe me, I don't know. Because I don't even know what period we are talking about and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you've answered the question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just in case it was the period that led you to say that you didn't know, I'm speaking of the period during the war, sir. Does that assist you in recalling what Mr. Simatovic's position was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: He was head of one administration, but I don't know which one it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And his deputy, that was Dragan Filipovic, also known as Fico; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Returning to your remarks, you next say that: "The concept of establishment of SNB is dated from the period when part of its personnel had noticed the intentions of Muslim-Croatian coalition. Understanding the politics of the SDS, they were taking part in certain activities on collecting and providing the information that was of importance for the Serbian population and its leadership. This staff," you say, "has helped to paralyse functions of the former MUP, especially of the former National Security Service." That's true information that you were providing to the RS Assembly; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes, but I have to explain this to you, that it wasn't from the State Security Service that I came to head the State Security Service. I came from public security. That's where I worked until 1991. So this is information that my chiefs of administration --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I hadn't asked about your career trajectory. This is information you got from your chiefs of administration and you provided truthfully to the RS Assembly; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Precisely. Because at that time, in 1991, I was not in the State Security Service, so I could not have been aware of this information. On the other hand, I'm the one who is submitting a report, but it's a group of people who drafted that report, and they probably worked on that earlier on. That's when they wrote it. I assumed that that is what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you say 1991, 1991 and the early part of 1992 is the period when, in your remarks, you were saying that understanding the politics of the SDS, these employees were taking part in certain activities and providing information that was of importance for the Serbian population and that they were paralysing the functions of the former MUP; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: What I've been trying to explain to you, that in 1991, in March, I was an employee of the centre of public security in Banja Luka and I worked on foreign affairs, affairs related to foreigners. And up until the moment --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I understand that. What I'm saying is, these remarks that you provided on the basis, you say, of reports from your chiefs of administration, these remarks that you provided to the RS Assembly, when you said that these SNB personnel had been paralysing the functions of the former MUP and had been providing information of importance to the Serbian population, that happened during 1991 and the beginning of 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Can I please take a look at that paragraph? Could you give me that paragraph so that I could see it, for the sake of the translation? If possible, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sure. It's the long paragraph on the left side. And if we can zoom in, you can see in the middle of the paragraph the letters "SDS" and so it immediately follows that as it did when I read it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Just a moment. Yes, I see that, SDS. Yes, now I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Are you able now to confirm that the period that you're describing in those remarks is 1991 and the beginning of 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 218 in the English and 238 in the B/C/S, in the middle of the page in the B/C/S we read you say -- and it's actually the middle in the English as well, you're describing the last -- the previous eight months. You say: "We forwarded 550 pieces of written information from the military domain to the Intelligence Security organ of the Main Staff of the Republika Srpska Army. In addition to aforementioned, on a daily basis intelligence has been exchanged with the State Security Service of Serbia. Thus, 295 pieces of written information have been forwarded in this period." And it's correct, as you say here, that you were sharing large quantities of information with both the VRS and DB Serbia; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: A lot less with the RS. I don't see the information here. I don't see whether this information is contained here. Could you please help me with this so that I don't waste any time. I cannot find it. I think there is no reference to the RSK here. Are you referring to the RSK?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No, I said the Main Staff of the Republika Srpska Army, which I read you say 550 pieces of information that had been shared and so I'd said "VRS." So you were sharing large quantities of information with both the VRS and DB Serbia; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd just ask that Mr. Kijac's remarks at this session be added to P2508 which is other excerpts from the session and we'll upload a new version containing these remarks as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Defence, of course, for contextualisation may add to that as well. Then we'll hear from you soon about a new upload to replace the previous selection. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 09558.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, take a look at the people in this photograph on your screen. Starting on the far left, that's Stojan Zupljanin, the head of CSB Banja Luka; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The next man is Mr. Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Then Momcilo Krajisnik; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And then Jovica Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: President Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Milan Martic from the RSK?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And then the man leaning on the chair Mr. Martic is sitting on, that's you; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recall the occasion when this photo was taken?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: I cannot say when exactly, but I think it's sometime in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recall what the seven of you were you meeting about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: I cannot say. I mean, probably I was accompanying the president on some trip. And I know that this picture was taken in Bijeljina, to the best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the people in this picture shared common goals during the war; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: A very difficult question for me. I really cannot give you an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, can we have 65 ter 33177.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is a card sent by Jovica Stanisic on Security Day 1994 to the MUP of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. And at the end of the document, he writes: "We are now entering the decisive phase of the fight to achieve the common goals of all the Serbian lands, more determined and prepared than ever before." And it's correct that Mr. Stanisic understood the Serbian lands to be the Republika Srpska, the Republic of Serbian Krajina, and the Republic of Serbia; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: I cannot say because I see from this document that it wasn't sent to Republika Srpska. It was sent to the Republic of the Serb Krajina. This is the first time I am seeing this document, so I really don't want to read all of it now and to interpret what it was that Mr. Stanisic was trying to say through this document. If you have a document that was sent to me, then I can certainly provide you with a comment. However, what I see here is the Republic of the Serb Krajina, the Ministry of the Interior, to the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You talked before, ten minutes ago maybe, about how at your level your contacts with DB Serbia, they would have to have been with the minister. You confirmed what you'd told the assembly, that you were exchanging hundreds of pieces of information with DB Serbia, and you testify now you've got no idea what Jovica Stanisic thought the Serbian lands were? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: I don't understand you or perhaps you did not understand me. Exchange of information is in written form. It's not that I go and talk to him over a cup of coffee about the political situation. I sent him information of the state security sector of Republika Srpska. Sometimes this was on a daily basis, sometimes on a weekly basis, sometimes on a fortnightly basis. I would see Mr. Stanisic every three or four months and we would not converse along those lines as to what Mr. Stanisic thought. I assume that if you asked Mr. Stanisic, he could not tell you what I was thinking at the time. So likewise, I cannot tell you what he was thinking.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's go step by step. We agree, I take it, that the Serbian lands include the Republic of Serbia; right? Everybody would have understood it that way at the time.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Again, you're putting this question to me. I am supposed to talk about who understood what and how people understood certain things, and I cannot do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If somebody had said to you in 1994: We're protecting the Serbian lands, what lands would you have understood them to mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Well, there is no denying that. But you're asking me about my thinking. I mean, I can talk about my own thinking, but I cannot give comments with regard to what Mr. Stanisic was thinking. If you're asking me what I thought, then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, what did you understand all the Serbian lands to mean? For yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, at that moment that was Republic of Srpska Krajina, Republika Srpska, and Republic of Serbia, naturally. But do not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. No --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 06830.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, one of the ways that the common goals Stanisic referred to or sometimes articulated was in terms of the ultimate aspiration of a united Serb state; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, the 65 ter number you asked for is not on the transcript. Can you repeat that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, it's 06830, and I appreciate the court officer having located it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll just put my question now that we have the document in the context of it. This is a New Year's card from Mr. Martic to Mr. Karadzic. He writes: "The year 1994 has been characterised by efforts to achieve united views towards a common goal - the creation of a united Serbian state." Now, this is one of the ways that the common goal that Jovica referred to in the previous document was sometimes articulated; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Again you're asking me something that I cannot answer. A moment ago I could not interpret documents, and now you're asking me to interpret documents. I cannot interpret what Mr. Martic meant by --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No, sir --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: -- what he wrote to Mr. Karadzic for the new year. I see it's 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm not asking you to interpret the document. I'm saying Mr. Martic says there is a common goal, the creation of a united Serbian state. That is one of the ways you yourself heard people at the time express the common goals of the people in that photograph we saw; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Again, I'm telling you, you can ask me about my position. I know what the position was of the state leadership of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: The Republika Srpska --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: -- should be self-reliant and I do not know about this --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the rest of what the witness is saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, perhaps we'll look at the state leadership of Republika Srpska's positions in more detail later. Is it your evidence, yes or no, that you heard people, including people in that photograph with you, during the war express the ultimate aspiration of a united Serb state? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Given my position, I could not talk to these people, bearing in mind --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- the ultimate political objective. Yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the simple question was whether you heard people, including those who were with you in that photograph, whether you heard them express the ultimate aspiration of a united Serb state. Did you hear that or did you not hear that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart to play a video now, 65 ter 27977a. The transcript has been confirmed by CLSS, so we only have to play it once. And just in case my speed was off, it was 27977a.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you say 27977a?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: There is no sound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you provided transcripts to the booth?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "RM: Mr. President, the Army of Republika Srpska is implementing your words from the last Assembly that Serbs (unintelligible) in a war brigade. I'm also here today, with these gentlemen from this area, and with these hard-working young men - soldiers, our workers, and professors. Here, among the reapers, there are intellectuals as well as common people. There are people here who have lost one or two of their closest family members, even their children (unintelligible) Republika Srpska. In the name of their blood and bones, I wish that our state, Republika Srpska, and the Serbian people flourish, in one country. May your words from the last Assembly session be broadcast through the media and be heard by all our people. Let us stand side by side and defeat this ill time. Let us overcome all the storms, the Scylla and Charybdis, and fulfil our dream that all the Serbs live in one country. Cheers and welcome among our soldiers and fighters."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Two questions to very briefly follow-up, sir. First, you agree that in that clip we saw General Mladic describing the ultimate aspiration of all Serbs in one state the same way that Mr. Martic did in the previous document; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: I heard this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And second, in light of the SRT, which I understand to be Serb Radio Television, logo on the screen, would you like to -- well, let me ask it this way: Has the broadcast of General Mladic expressing a goal this way refreshed your recollection as to whether Serb leaders expressed the goal of the creation of a united Serbian state during the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Well, I can just confirm that I heard this. Again, I cannot confirm what Serb leaders, as you had put it, had in their minds. You can play this video-clip, I can confirm that it's authentic. Now, what was in somebody's head -- well, you have to understand that my position as head of the State Security Sector was not a political post. After all, I was somebody who was engaged in operative work, from the security field. I'm not a politician. I do not attend assembly meetings unless invited. And, also, I don't attend Main Board meetings because I'm not a member of the SDS and I do not hold any party position within the SDS, so you do have to understand me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, at the moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, I'm looking at the clock. We really have to take the break now because otherwise there will be hardly any time left. One second.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I did have one follow-up which I can put either before or after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, can we take the break now?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll take a break. We would like to see you back in 20 minutes, and we'll resume at 10 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, just a brief follow-up on exhibits from the last session. The full English translation for 65 ter 17058a, P7576 MFI, has been uploaded into e-court under doc ID FI2005910A-ET. And we'd ask that the court officer be instructed to replace the current translation with the full translation and we'd ask that the document be admitted. And that's the first document, the appointment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you mean page 2 now being part of it as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, you are hereby instructed to replace the existing English translation of P7576 by the newly uploaded one as just referred to by Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And then I'd tender the other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then P7576, as now newly uploaded, is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And I'd tender the other unadmitted documents I used. First, the photograph, 65 ter 09558.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document number 09558 receives Exhibit Number P7577, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7577 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Second, 65 ter 33177, the Security Day card from Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 33177 receives Exhibit Number P7578.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7578 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: 65 ter 06830, the New Year's Day card from Martic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives Exhibit Number P7579.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7579 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And 65 ter 27977a, the SRT video of General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives Exhibit Number P7580, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7580 is admitted into evidence, and I see that the CD has just been handed over. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to turn now to Arkan, who you referred to in paragraph 65 of your statement. Now, you say that Arkan and his unit came to Bijeljina and Zvornik in 1992, and he had contacts with official organs of BH and the SFRY. When you say he had contacts with official organs of BH, you mean official organs of the Republika Srpska; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: I don't think you paraphrased it well. I had in mind the leadership of Bosnia-Herzegovina. As far as I know, in 1992, in Bijeljina, he met with Mr. Fikret Abdic, who was a member of the presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and with Ms. Biljana Plavsic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And can we have 65 ter 02362, page 20 in both languages. And my speed may have been off, it's 02362.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see at the top of the page in the B/C/S the end of Ms. Plavsic's remarks. In those remarks, she says: "I sent letters to all addresses. My intention was to pay anybody who was willing to fight for the Serbian cause and gather them around, so letters were sent out. You talk about paramilitary and non-paramilitary formations. You will have to excuse me, that has nothing to do with me. I was looking for the people who are willing to fight for the Serbian cause, who are willing to fight in the territory of Republika Srpska. The letters were sent to the Soviet Union, to Seselj, Arkan, and Jovic. Do as you like, accuse me now if you want. I want to make it clear, because this is second time, Minister, it's not hearsay, I did do it, and you can judge me if you want." Now, you're aware, aren't you, that Arkan had also had contact with official organs of the RS before he arrived in Bijeljina, that in fact he arrived there at Ms. Plavsic's invitation, as it says here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Could you please scroll up the page in B/C/S, because I don't see the beginning of Ms. Plavsic's contribution. Still, I don't see it. In any case, it doesn't matter. First you have to tell me when and where this was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no. I think let's first of all -- if the witness asked to be able to read that, you now can see it at the bottom of the page, the first three lines.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mm-hmm, I see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then -- have you read that? Then we'll move to the next page in B/C/S. Now, you were not asked about when and where she said this, but you were asked about whether you were aware of Arkan coming to Bijeljina, being invited to come there by Ms. Plavsic. Are you aware of that or are you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm not aware of it. As far as I see, it was an assembly session --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, that's not -- it was read to you as words apparently spoken by Madam Plavsic. Mr. Traldi, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, she also mentions Seselj, that's Vojislav Seselj, the leader of the Serb Radical Party; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: He also sent volunteers to Bosnia; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: There were such formations which called themselves Seselj's Men, but I don't know where they came from. I think they were from our area but were members of the Serb Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Jovic, that's Mirko Jovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And he was head of the Serb Renewal Movement; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: I think you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And also sent volunteers to Bosnia; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: I don't have that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask that Ms. Plavsic's remarks be added to P7196. As with the previous assembly, we'll upload a new version including them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll wait for a number. And then after that, the Defence, as always, has an opportunity to further contextualise the portion you have added, and then we'll decide on replacing the newly uploaded version by the existing one. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart to play another video now. This one's from French TV in 1991, 65 ter 22456b. And again, it's been confirmed so we only have to play it once.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: "We don't take any more prisoners. We are going to kill every fascist soldier we catch. They have to know that."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the speaker we saw there, that was Arkan; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And he was known to be a criminal during the war; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes, I would say he was of security interest to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender that clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 22456b receives Exhibit Number P7581.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7581 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P364, page 49. And, sorry, 49 in both the B/C/S transcript and in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, this is one of General Mladic's notebooks from the war. We're looking here at his notes of a meeting on the 22nd of September, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we turn to page 52 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'll see General Milovanovic begin to speak --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now we have also English on the left-hand side of the screen. That should be B/C/S but the typed transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we turn now to page 53.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Milovanovic mentions at the top of the page in the B/C/S: "A team from DB Serbia, Filipovic and Bozovic, as well as Kijac and Kovac." Now, that's Filipovic, Frenki's deputy who we discussed earlier; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Bozovic is Rade Bozovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: I don't think his first name was Rade, if we have the same person in mind. Or perhaps it is his real name.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What name did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: I don't think it was Rade. I can't recall it off the cuff. I think it is Rajo Bozovic, but I don't know his real first name. I think we have the same person in mind. But when you said Rade, I'm not sure that was his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's check if we have the same person in mind on the next couple of names. Kijac, that's you; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Kovac would be Tomo Kovac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes, the deputy minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And then Mladic records that General Milovanovic mentions that 300 fighters of -- well, that 1200 fighters would come and be incorporated into the 1st Krajina Corps and be used like all other units, and says: "300 Arkan's volunteers arrived and were put into the RS MUP ..." Now, you mention Arkan's deployment in late 1995 in your statement. You don't mention that you were involved in co-ordinating that deployment with the VRS, but that's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by "co-ordination." I did know Arkan was there, but I had no authority. Here you can see at what point he was included or became involved. I did know that he was in the area of Krajina in 1995 and that there were some 300 or so people. I think that there were fewer, though. I think there were 200. It all happened at the time when some of the municipalities fell. There was a scheme from the Serbian DB and apparently Kijac and Kovac were a part of that. It was possible that I was present at some meetings, but I could not have co-ordinated his arrival. It was not within my competence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's possible you were present at meetings about their deployment or is it the truth that you were present at meetings about their deployment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: I definitely did not attend the meetings where their arrival was discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 33293. And I'll be very brief about it. I see the time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a commendation given to Arkan by Karadzic after the war. Were you aware that this known criminal was decorated after the war by the president of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Not after the war. I think his guards were decorated, but I see this for the first time. I didn't think he received it but the guards. It wasn't he that received it in his own name. What year is this?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I see a handwritten date there, the 30th of May, 1996. Do you see that too, sir? And it's in the lower left.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC
utterances.text: Yes, I see it now. I'm not aware of it, in 1996. I do know that there was some decoration given in 1995 when they were supposed to leave the Republika Srpska. I think it was in Bijeljina, to the best of my recollection. I wasn't aware that he was -- he received this in his own name.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender the document and I think for me that's a convenient time to break for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 33293 receives Exhibit Number P7582.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7582 is admitted. Witness, we'll adjourn for the day and we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 in the morning. But before we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm addressing you. Will we -- how much time would you still need, Mr. Traldi, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think I've used about an hour. I think I'll stay within the time I'd estimated, which was three and a half, even with the additional time on direct. But I'd have to check to be sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lukic, what do you suggest for tomorrow? We'll first go to the evidence of this witness or would you rather start with the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, I discussed with Mr. Kijac and he agreed that we should start with another witness who --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- prefers to finish his --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that witness is scheduled for how long?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Give me one second. Two and a half and two, 45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that certainly means we'll not --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Finish tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- finish that tomorrow. And possibly we'll resume, then, on Wednesday morning the testimony of this witness -- of the present witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, we'll finish with the next one first. There is almost --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but we'll resume somewhere during the Wednesday morning -- or at least there is a chance?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is a chance, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then, Mr. Kijac, first of all, I would like to instruct you that you should not speak or communicate when -- with whomever about your testimony, whether that is testimony you've given already or testimony still to be given. Tomorrow you -- we'll hear the evidence of another witness, and that may continue -- it's likely to continue until Wednesday, but perhaps during the morning of Wednesday you may be -- we may resume hearing your evidence. Now, we'll keep you informed through the Victims and Witness Section on -- at what time you should make yourself available on standby on Wednesday morning or even that it would be only on Thursday that we would need you. So please carefully follow the instructions given to you by VWS which will come most likely later tomorrow or even in the morning of Wednesday, if that's clear to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No speaking aloud, Mr. Mladic. You know that. We'll adjourn for the day and we'll resume tomorrow, Tuesday, 20th of October, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I. And I had forgotten that that will be a relatively short session because we'll -- or at least the hearing will end at 12.00. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 20th day of October, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.21 p.m.,
